rounds.text: Share Samadhan Ltd demonstrates powerful top-line expansion, led by a 3-year compounded sales growth of 31% [E12], alongside robust screen reasons highlighting sales up 39% year-on-year [E49] and net profit surging 119% year-on-year [E51]. Operational execution is clearly snapping back to life, evidenced by a dramatic quarterly operating margin jump to 46% in September 2026 compared to 29% in the prior-year quarter [E21], while recent results score a perfect 100 out of 100 with accelerating performance [E56]. Furthermore, the company is backed by a rock-solid balance sheet featuring a negligible debt-to-equity ratio of 0.01x [E27], borrowings reduced to a mere Rs 0.25 Cr [E29], and a highly comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 10.10x [E28]. Operating in a financial services sector that enjoys a positive tailwind score of +0.77 [E57], the company maintains a stable promoter holding of 62.52% [E31], ensuring strong alignment with long-term equity holders. Conceded: [E35], [E36], [E47].

Share Samadhan Ltd carries severe underlying risks and a valuation that is fundamentally unsupported by its cash generation. The company’s operating cash flow for March 2026 is deeply negative at Rs -11.36 Cr, driving an alarming cash conversion ratio of -25.24x against reported profit [E24, E25]. This is compounded by a catastrophic ballooning of working capital days from 558 days to 1,249 days alongside excessively high debtors of 412 days [E46, E47]. Consequently, free cash flow sits firmly in the red at Rs -14.42 Cr [E26]. From a valuation standpoint, the stock trades at a steep P/E of 78.23x against a sector benchmark of 18.53x [E6], while a discounted cash flow model estimates intrinsic value at just Rs 30 per share compared to the current market price of Rs 44.6, leaving a negative margin of safety of -47.8% [E35, E36]. Furthermore, institutional confidence has evaporated, evidenced by foreign institutions slashing their holding from 6.56% to 0.55% and domestic institutions completely exiting from 4.73% to 0.00% over a two-year period [E32, E33]. Profitability metrics also look weak on a trailing basis, with a meager 1.5% ROE and 1.6% ROCE reported in filed statements [E10, E11], accompanied by earnings that rely on Rs 1.35 Cr of other income [E45]. Conceded: [E21], [E27], [E51].

Conceded: [E24], [E25], [E26]. The bear highlights negative operating and free cash flow for March 2026, but overlooks the company's pristine solvency profile with a nearly debt-free structure at 0.01x debt to equity and negligible borrowings of Rs 0.25 Cr [E27, E29]. While the bear cites high P/E and a DCF overvaluation of -47.8%, the fundamental valuation is actually far more reasonable at a 20.4x P/E and a modest 1.25x price-to-book ratio on filed statements [E1, E2]. The bear targets institutional exits [E32, E33], yet ignores that promoters have steadfastly held their majority 62.52% stake [E31]. Furthermore, the bear's trailing profitability concerns [E10, E11] miss the powerful accelerating turnaround highlighted by a massive 119% year-on-year net profit surge and surging quarterly operating margins hitting 46% in September 2026 [E21, E51, E56]. Conceded: [E46], [E47].

Conceded: [E27], [E29], [E31]. While promoters hold 62.52% [E31] and debt is low [E27, E29], a pristine balance sheet does not neutralize severe operational cash burn where operating cash flow plunged to negative Rs 11.36 Cr and free cash flow dropped to negative Rs 14.42 Cr in March 2026 [E25, E26]. The bull defends the valuation using a 20.4x P/E [E1], but the data provider metrics peg the P/E at an alarming 78.23x against a sector benchmark of just 18.53x [E6]. Furthermore, the bull leans heavily on a 119% net profit surge [E51, E56], yet trailing twelve-month sales growth has collapsed by -38% [E13] alongside catastrophic working capital degradation where debtor days sit at 412 days and working capital days ballooned from 558 to 1,249 days [E46, E47]. Conceded: [E51]. Finally, the DCF overvaluation of -47.8% and the reverse DCF requirement for 12.1% growth when base assumptions only support 7.0% prove that current market pricing demands an unrealistic trajectory unsupported by the underlying cash flows [E35, E36, E37].
